data.name: The Superfluous
data.detailed_description:
"The Superfluous" [soo-pur-floo-uh s] A cave-diving, sci-fi, rogue-lite, platformer with jet packs and lots of explosions. Help stop an apocalyptic asteroid on collision course with Earth. Lead a squad to the center of the asteroid and blast it into space dust.
 

features


  • Rogue - Levels are randomly generated and get progressively harder as the player progresses through them. The player's goal is to defeat a boss to unlock the next biome.
  • Perma-Death - for the individual characters, but they are cloned back to level 0 and can be used for other missions.
  • Perma-Progress - any upgrades the player purchases or any checkpoints the player reaches are saved. If a mission fails all loot will be lost. The player must decide to leave the dungeon and keep their loot or continue to the next level.
  • Co-Op - Play the campaign with a friend in local co-op.
  • Arena Mode - Challenge up to 3 of you friends in a 4 player local arena mode (WIP).
  • Platformer - side scrolling 2D platformer. The main locomotion of the player is walking and using a jet-pack. Attacking is done in two to four directions (depending on the weapon equipped).
  • Squad Based - Never journey alone! Bring along several squad mates with different tools and weapons to help you dive deeper. Balance your squad with miners, healers, heavy weaponry and explosives.
  • Destructible Terrain - mine and blow your way through the level to collect gems, create a shortcut, or gain an advantage over your enemies.
  • Progression - As squad member kill enemies and clear cave sectors they gain XP. When they gain enough XP the go up a level and a random perk is assigned. These will be lost on death and can be changed for gold back at base.
  • Three Biomes - explore the 'Dark Cave', 'The Underwater', or the 'Lava' biomes on your quest to save the world.
  • Economy - Loot can be obtained in the form of Gold and Gems. Gold is used to buy new crew DNA (unlock characters) and re-rolling perks. Gems are used to upgrade your gear, the number of people in your squad, the starting health of characters, etc.
  • Story - a fun, light story about the impending destruction of earth, bureaucracy, the military and sci-fi culture.
  • Local CO-OP - 2 (shooting for 4) player local multiplayer. A holo-deck 'arena' is planned to add death-match gameplay.
  • Controller Support - This game was designed for both keyboard/mouse and controller support.
  • Sci-Fi - I love reading all types of science fiction {Asimov, Niven, Heinlein, Card, Howey, Clark, Wells, etc.} and have always tried to include that genre in my games.

 

the story


All games should have a story. A story can motivate and inspire or just be something fun and entertaining. In The Superfluous, we are shooting for the later. I know, I know, Indie games should make us feel something to be 'successful' (or so it seems to me nowadays); and we enjoy games with really in-depth emotional stories... but sometimes we all just want to laugh and blow stuff up.

The year is 2121. Scientists have discovered an asteroid (BAR-101), half the size of the moon, on a collision course with Earth. Normally this would cause great distress for the people of Earth, but because this asteroid will not make impact for another 1,000 years, most deem it as not important. Although there remain a few people that are concerned(a fringe political group formally called Republicans). To appease this minority group, the government of Earth spent billions of dollars to send a space shuttle to BAR-101. The shuttle crew’s mission is to place a Zero-Point-Energy bomb at the center of the asteroid and destroy it before it reaches Earth.

The shuttle, your shuttle, is named “The UWN Superfluous”. This ship is equipped with state of the art cloning technology, in case you or your crew is met with an unfortunate end before the mission is complete. New crew DNA profiles are available for purchase in exchange for any valuable metal (gold) found on BAR-101.*

Your ship also has a research lab to upgrade your equipment using any minerals available. Though please note the upgrades are super expensive and don’t really make your gear that much more effective.

Your crew will be equipped with our most advanced environmental suits and super sweet jet packs to help them navigate through BAR-101’s many caves, chasms, crevices, crooks, and caverns.

You have approximately 999 years to complete your mission, so no procrastination. Remember the fate of the world might rest with you and your crew. Though popular consensus says we will either kill ourselves through nuclear war, a super virus, or by proving to aliens we are useless/dangerous to the rest of the galaxy.**

  • While you were in cryo-sleep the funding for this mission was cut in lieu of nicer toilet seats.
  • *Consensus made through a social media poll.

 

environments/biomes


Very quickly you'll find out your mission is not what it seems. You were expecting a lifeless rock your team would spend a few easy years drilling through. BAR-101 was anything but. Riddled with caves and things that love the taste of your EXO suits, the asteroid, and your mission will be anything but easy.

Dark Cave - Fight bats, slimes, 4 legged spiders and more as you pick your way through the first 'Dark Cave' Biome. You'll see mostly gray rocks but strange fireflies will also light up the cave with a strange ambiance.

The Underwater - Deeper down you find there is a large pocket of water trapped under the 'Dark Cave' biome. 'The Underwater' challenges the player with slowed down movement. Imagine deep sea divers in their large brass suits. Players will face rocket fish, sneaky swordfish, methane gas bubbles, butt-pinching crabs, and more as they delve deeper within the asteroid.

Lava Zone - The last of the three biomes is where the asteroid gets its life-giving heat. The lava zone adds the extra danger of overheating the players EXO suit. If the player stays on the ground too long the heat will damage the player. Enemies like the Splitting Fire Slime, the Fire Spitting Spider, falling rocks, and flame shooting fissures will try to abate the player.

 

meet the Team


Adam Truncale - Lead Programmer
Melissa Truncale - story and Marketing
Andrew Dees - Music and Soundtrack
Alex Lazar - Artist and Box/concept Art

data.short_description: "The Superfluous" [soo-pur-floo-uh s] A cave-diving, sci-fi, rogue-lite, platformer with jet packs and lots of explosions. Help stop an apocalyptic asteroid on collision course with Earth. Lead a squad to the center of the asteroid and blast it into space dust.

reviews.review:
The Superfluous is a science-fiction roguelite action platformer developed and published by Voided Pixels, combining procedural cave exploration, squad management systems, destructible terrain, and fast-paced traversal into a unique independent experience that blends multiple genres together. Rather than focusing purely on platforming precision or combat intensity, the game builds much of its identity around experimentation, strategic planning, and adapting to unpredictable environments. Its systems-heavy approach creates an experience that feels ambitious, occasionally chaotic, but consistently interesting for players who enjoy overcoming challenges through preparation and flexibility.

The game introduces an unusual futuristic premise centered around a distant threat that humanity struggles to take seriously. In the year 2121, scientists discover a massive asteroid called BAR-101 moving toward Earth. Despite the danger, the impact remains far enough into the future that urgency becomes lost within bureaucracy and political hesitation. Players become part of a mission aboard the UWN Superfluous, assigned to travel toward the asteroid and destroy it before catastrophe becomes unavoidable. What initially begins as a straightforward operation slowly develops into a stranger and more dangerous expedition as hidden threats buried deep within the asteroid begin to reveal themselves.

One of the strongest aspects of The Superfluous comes from how effectively it combines exploration and squad management. Players are not simply controlling a single character moving through levels. Instead, team composition becomes a major strategic consideration. Different specialists bring different advantages into missions, creating decisions that influence how players approach combat, exploration, and survival. Some crew members excel at support roles while others provide stronger offensive tools or environmental utility.

The procedural cave systems become the central stage where these mechanics come together. Each descent into the asteroid creates new layouts filled with hazards, enemies, and opportunities. Memorization rarely guarantees success because environmental arrangements continuously shift. Adaptation becomes one of the most valuable skills, forcing players to respond dynamically rather than relying entirely on routine.

Movement mechanics contribute heavily to the game’s identity. Jetpack traversal changes how players interact with environments, allowing movement across vertical spaces while creating faster and more flexible exploration opportunities. Navigating dangerous terrain becomes increasingly satisfying as movement systems begin feeling more natural. Momentum management and positioning quickly evolve into essential survival skills.

Combat also benefits from environmental interaction systems. The destructible terrain mechanics allow players to shape portions of the environment directly through explosives and specialized equipment. Rather than moving through fixed pathways exclusively, players gain freedom to create alternate routes, uncover hidden areas, and gain tactical advantages through environmental manipulation. This system strengthens player creativity while helping progression remain unpredictable.

Permanent progression systems create satisfying long-term momentum. Individual failures carry consequences, but larger upgrades remain available across future attempts. This balance helps maintain challenge without making failure feel overly punishing. Every run contributes toward broader advancement, reinforcing the roguelite structure while encouraging experimentation.

Enemy encounters gradually evolve alongside environmental complexity. New dangers appear deeper inside the asteroid, forcing players to reconsider strategies and adapt squad composition accordingly. The escalating difficulty helps maintain tension effectively while supporting the sense that deeper exploration carries greater risk.

One particularly enjoyable aspect comes from the game’s humor. Despite the larger stakes involving planetary destruction, The Superfluous frequently embraces satire and absurdity throughout its worldbuilding. Elements involving bureaucracy, political indecision, and exaggerated science-fiction themes create personality that separates the experience from more serious survival adventures. The lighter tone helps strengthen atmosphere without disrupting progression.

Visually, the game adopts pixel-art presentation that prioritizes readability and gameplay clarity. Environmental effects, explosions, and destructible terrain provide satisfying visual feedback during combat and exploration. While presentation occasionally reveals limitations associated with smaller-scale independent development, the visual style supports gameplay effectively.

The game does carry some rough edges. Procedural systems occasionally generate particularly demanding situations where enemy placement and environmental hazards combine into frustrating encounters. Certain mechanics also require adjustment before fully clicking together, particularly movement systems that initially feel unusual.

Longer sessions may reveal repetitive elements as progression structures begin repeating familiar patterns. However, procedural variety and strategic decision-making generally provide enough variation to maintain engagement across multiple attempts.

What makes The Superfluous stand apart is its willingness to experiment. Voided Pixels creates an experience that occasionally feels larger than its production scale but remains compelling because of its ambition. The combination of procedural exploration, squad management, destructible environments, and movement-focused gameplay gives the adventure a distinctive identity.

For players who enjoy roguelites, systems-driven progression, exploration-heavy action games, and platformers that reward experimentation rather than rigid mastery alone, The Superfluous delivers a memorable independent experience filled with challenge, creativity, and enough variety to encourage repeated exploration.

Rating: 7/10
